newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse turnover down in week to May 30.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse turnover down in week to May 30.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) reported on Monday a 12.7 percent decline in its turnover during the week ending May 30 on a lack of secondary market activity.
Total turnover fell to 52.388 million dinars ($9.33 million) from 65.091 million dinars a week ago. The number of transactions rose to 209 from 183, the BSE said.
The entire activity was performed on the primary market, the bourse said.

"Market liquidity was no better and no worse than in the previous week, but there was no secondary market activity with the central bank selling bonds from its portfolio," BSE spokesman Milko Stimac told Reuters.
For the week ending May 30, the BSE reported the following details:
* Commercial paper traded 193 times for a volume of 26.438 million dinars.
* Treasury bills accounted for seven transactions worth 1.53 million dinars.
Interest rates on commercial paper and treasury bills ranged between 9.00 and 13.50 percent per month while maturity stood between seven and 30 days.
* There was one transaction in the central bank short-term bonds worth two million dinars.
* The bourse reported three deals in the state T-bills worth 22.1 million dinars.
* BSE reported no sale of bonds from the central bank's portfolio. The National Bank of Yugoslavia has been active over last several weeks selling bonds issued by the Serbian Commodity
